words.definition: A pattern, phrase, or rhyme used to help someone remember information easily.
words.example: To recall the planets in order, she taught us a silly mnemonic about pizza.
words.mnemonic: The opening M is silent, like in 'knee' — a quiet aid to your memory.

words.definition: A partial or total loss of the ability to recall past events.
words.example: After the crash he had amnesia and couldn't even name his own children.
words.mnemonic: Break it down: 'a-' (without) + 'mnesis' (memory) = without memory.

words.definition: A person who has lost the ability to recall past experiences.
words.example: The amnesiac wandered the train station, unable to say where he lived.
words.mnemonic: Amnesia plus '-ac' names the sufferer, just like 'maniac' names one who has mania.

words.definition: The act of calling things back from the past, especially a patient's medical history.
words.example: During the anamnesis, the doctor asked about every illness he'd had since boyhood.
words.mnemonic: 'ana-' (back) + 'mnesis' (memory) = drawing memory back up to the surface.

words.definition: The state of being completely forgotten, or of total unawareness.
words.example: Once a household name, the singer faded into oblivion within a single decade.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'oblivious' — both describe being blank to and blanked from the world.

words.definition: The gradual process of losing one's grip on things once known.
words.example: Old age brought a quiet obliviscence, familiar names slipping away one by one.
words.mnemonic: Same root as 'oblivion' and 'oblivious' — picture facts sliding off a slick surface.

words.definition: To think and talk fondly about pleasant events from one's past.
words.example: The old friends reminisced for hours about their reckless college road trips.
words.mnemonic: 're-' (again) + a 'mind' sound = to bring the past to mind once more.

words.definition: A fondly recounted memory or story about something from earlier times.
words.example: Her reminiscence of wartime London kept the whole dinner table spellbound.
words.mnemonic: The noun of 'reminisce' — a single polished piece of the past, handed to a listener.

words.definition: Suggesting or calling to mind something from an earlier time.
words.example: The smell of warm pine was reminiscent of childhood holidays in the mountains.
words.mnemonic: Cousin of 'reminisce' — it's the quality of a thing that makes you reminisce.

words.definition: To honor an important person or event with a ceremony or lasting tribute.
words.example: A bronze statue was raised to commemorate the sailors lost at sea.
words.mnemonic: 'com-' (together) + 'memor' (memory) = a whole community remembering together.

words.definition: To create something lasting that keeps a person or event in people's minds.
words.example: The town memorialized its founder by naming the new library after her.
words.mnemonic: 'memorial' + '-ize' = to turn something into a memorial.

words.definition: Tending to bring vivid feelings, memories, or images strongly to mind.
words.example: The poem was so evocative that readers could almost taste the salt sea air.
words.mnemonic: Built from 'evoke' — describes anything that evokes a rush of feeling.

words.definition: To call up a feeling, memory, or image in someone's mind.
words.example: One bar of that old song can evoke the summer we first met.
words.mnemonic: 'e-' (out) + 'voke' (voice, as in 'vocal') = to call something out into the open.

words.definition: To bring a past fact or experience back into one's mind.
words.example: I can't quite recollect where I left my keys after last night's party.
words.mnemonic: 're-' (again) + 'collect' = gathering scattered thoughts back together again.

words.definition: A wistful, sentimental longing for happy times or places from one's past.
words.example: Flipping through the old photo album filled her with nostalgia for her hometown.
words.mnemonic: Greek 'nostos' (homecoming) + 'algia' (pain) = the sweet ache to return home.

words.definition: Feeling a wistful longing for happy times in the past.
words.example: Flipping through the old yearbook made her nostalgic for lazy summer afternoons.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'nose-tragic' — your nose gets teary and tragic remembering the good old days. (Greek nostos 'homecoming' + algos 'pain'.)

words.definition: The act of looking back on events or experiences from earlier.
words.example: In quiet retrospection, he saw how a handful of small choices had shaped his whole career.
words.mnemonic: retro- 'backward' + spect 'look' — like watching a retro film, you look back in time.

words.definition: Looking back on or concerned with past events or situations.
words.example: The gallery mounted a retrospective show covering forty years of the artist's work.
words.mnemonic: retro (backward) + spective (a spectacle) — a spectacle turned backward to the past.

words.definition: To rub or wipe something out until it can no longer be seen.
words.example: Centuries of rain had effaced the names carved into the old tombstones.
words.mnemonic: ef- + face — strip the 'face' off something, wiping its surface clean.

words.definition: To remove or blot out something completely, especially from a record.
words.example: The judge agreed to expunge the arrest from his file once probation ended.
words.mnemonic: ex- 'out' + 'punge' sounds like sponge — sponge it out completely.

words.definition: Impossible to wipe away, erase, or forget.
words.example: The disaster left an ineffaceable mark on everyone who lived through it.
words.mnemonic: in- 'not' + effaceable — the face simply won't come off, no matter how hard you scrub.

words.definition: Existing so long that its origin lies beyond anyone's knowledge or record.
words.example: From time immemorial, the villagers had gathered at the well each dawn.
words.mnemonic: im- 'not' + memorial — older than any memorial anyone could ever raise to it.

words.definition: A supposed physical trace left in the brain by an experience or memory.
words.example: Neuroscientists spent years hunting for the engram that stored the rat's fear of the cage.
words.mnemonic: en- 'in' + gram 'something written' — a telegram written into your brain tissue.

words.definition: Able to hold or keep things, especially facts in the mind.
words.example: Her remarkably retentive memory let her recite the whole poem after a single reading.
words.mnemonic: retain + -tive — a retentive tank is one that keeps the water in.

words.definition: To summarize the main points of something said or done before.
words.example: Before the vote, the chair paused to recapitulate the key arguments on both sides.
words.mnemonic: re- 'again' + capitul 'head/chapter' — go back over the main headings; it's just a 'recap'.

words.definition: An object surviving from the past, valued for its age or associations.
words.example: The rusted sword was a relic from a battle fought two hundred years ago.
words.mnemonic: From Latin relinquere 'to leave behind' (like 'relinquish') — a relic is what got left behind.

words.definition: The small part that remains after the rest is removed or used up.
words.example: After the water evaporated, a chalky residuum coated the bottom of the beaker.
words.mnemonic: Say 'residue' with a fancy Latin -uum ending — the leftover lump at the bottom.

words.definition: To press a mark onto a surface, or fix something firmly in the mind.
words.example: The child's boots imprinted a trail of little stars across the fresh snow.
words.mnemonic: im- 'onto' + print — to print a mark straight onto a surface.

words.definition: To write, carve, or engrave words onto a surface.
words.example: The jeweler offered to inscribe their initials inside the wedding band.
words.mnemonic: in- 'in' + scribe 'writer' — a scribe writes it right into the material.

words.definition: Words that have been carved or written onto a surface or in a book.
words.example: The inscription on the old coin was too worn to read.
words.mnemonic: in + script — the script set into stone, metal, or a title page.

words.definition: The act of grasping new ideas by relating them to what one already knows.
words.example: Her rich apperception let each new fact slot neatly into the framework of everything she had studied before.
words.mnemonic: 'appear' + 'perception' — new things appear to your perception through the lens of what you already understand.

words.definition: To generate or form new concepts, especially during creative brainstorming.
words.example: The design team gathered at the whiteboard to ideate freely before committing to a single prototype.
words.mnemonic: idea + -ate ('to make') — literally to make ideas.

words.definition: A dazed condition in which someone can barely think, move, or respond.
words.example: After his third sleepless night he wandered the office in a stupor, missing questions asked twice.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'stupid' + 'poor' — too dazed to think straight.

words.definition: Extreme weakness or emptiness caused by lack of food or nourishment.
words.example: The stranded hikers grew so weak from inanition that lifting a canteen took all their strength.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'in-a-nothing' — nothing in the stomach leaves you drained.

words.definition: Gradually falling out of use and passing out of date.
words.example: Fax machines were already obsolescent when the office finally replaced them with scanners.
words.mnemonic: -escent means 'becoming' (like adolescent becoming adult) — so becoming out of date.

words.definition: To make someone gradually accustomed to a situation through repeated exposure.
words.example: Lifeguards habituate themselves to the cold sea by wading in a little longer each morning.
words.mnemonic: Contains 'habit' — repeat something until it becomes a habit.

words.definition: To toughen or accustom someone to hardship so it no longer bothers them.
words.example: Years on the trauma ward had inured the nurse to sights that made visitors faint.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'in-endure' — being in it long enough that you can endure it.

words.definition: To fade gradually from sight or memory until nothing remains.
words.example: The morning mist began to evanesce as the sun climbed above the ridge.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'ever-vanish' — like a wisp of vapor thinning into air.

words.definition: To pass gradually out of use and stop being needed.
words.example: Streaming caused the corner DVD rental store to obsolesce within just a few years.
words.mnemonic: -esce = 'to become'; so it means to become old and unused (the verb cousin of obsolescent).

words.definition: To continue existing over a long time despite change or difficulty.
words.example: Roman roads perdure to this day, still bearing foot traffic after two thousand years.
words.mnemonic: per- ('through') + dure ('to last,' as in durable) — to last all the way through.

words.definition: Able to recall images with extraordinary, photograph-like vividness and detail.
words.example: With her eidetic memory she could recite the page number and exact wording of any passage.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'I-detect-it' — you detect every detail; from Greek eidos, 'form' or 'image.'

words.definition: Impossible to remove, destroy, or wipe out completely.
words.example: The scandal left an ineradicable stain on his reputation that no apology could wash away.
words.mnemonic: in- ('not') + eradicable (from eradicate, 'to root out') — cannot be rooted out.

words.definition: To destroy or root out something completely, leaving nothing behind.
words.example: The program aimed to extirpate the invasive weed before it could choke the native plants.
words.mnemonic: ex- + stirp (Latin for 'root') — to pull out by the roots.

words.definition: To censor or black out sensitive parts of a document before releasing it.
words.example: Officials redacted the informant's name from the report before handing it to reporters.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'red act' — a red marker acting to black out the lines.

words.definition: A state of temporary suspension or pause, awaiting later action or resolution.
words.example: The renovation plans were held in abeyance until the city finally approved the permits.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'a-bay-ance' — a ship kept at bay, waiting, going nowhere for now.

words.definition: The act of using the brain to think, reason, or work through ideas.
words.example: The chess grandmaster sat motionless for an hour, his intense cerebration invisible to the restless crowd.
words.mnemonic: Contains 'cerebr-' as in cerebrum, the brain — cerebration is the brain in action.

words.definition: Aimless daydreaming or letting the mind wander instead of paying attention.
words.example: "Stop your woolgathering and answer the question," the teacher snapped as I stared out the window.
words.mnemonic: Picture a shepherd so lost in dreams he wanders about gathering stray tufts of wool — going nowhere.

words.definition: Able to keep working hard for a long time without becoming tired.
words.example: The indefatigable nurse worked her third straight shift and still greeted each patient with a smile.
words.mnemonic: 'in-' (not) + 'de-fatigue-able' — literally not able to be fatigued.

words.definition: Showing great care, effort, and persistence in doing something.
words.example: Her assiduous note-taking meant she never missed a single detail from the lectures.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'a-SIT-uous' — someone who sits down and sticks at the task without budging.

words.definition: Working steadily and diligently with constant attention to a task.
words.example: Through sedulous practice, the young violinist mastered a passage that once seemed impossible.
words.mnemonic: 'Sed' sounds like 'said' — a sedulous worker does what needs to be said, over and over, faithfully.

words.definition: To take the place of something older, replacing it as better or more current.
words.example: The new safety regulations supersede all previous guidelines, so discard the old manual.
words.mnemonic: 'super' + 'sede' (sit) — the newcomer sits above, in the seat of the old one.

words.definition: To send someone or something to a lower or less important position.
words.example: After the losing season, the team was relegated to the second division.
words.mnemonic: 'Re-LEG-ate' — imagine being sent to the back of the LEG-room, demoted to the worst seat.

words.definition: To scold or rebuke someone harshly and severely.
words.example: The coach objurgated the players in the locker room until several hung their heads in shame.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'object' + 'berate' — you object loudly and berate the offender.

words.definition: Harshness or roughness of tone, manner, or temper.
words.example: "I never asked for your help," she replied with such asperity that the room fell silent.
words.mnemonic: Related to 'asperous' (rough) — think of rough sandpaper rubbing you the wrong way.

words.definition: Sharp bitterness of speech, mood, or taste.
words.example: The critic's review was written with an acerbity that left the director fuming for days.
words.mnemonic: Shares a root with 'acerbic' and 'acid' — the sour, biting taste of a bitter remark.

words.definition: A written record of events arranged in the order they happened.
words.example: Her diary became a chronicle of the small town's slow disappearance over fifty years.
words.mnemonic: 'Chron-' means time (as in chronological) — a record laid out in time order.

words.definition: Words written in memory of a dead person, often carved on a gravestone.
words.example: His epitaph read simply, "He made others laugh," and mourners smiled through their tears.
words.mnemonic: 'Epi-' (upon) + 'taph' (tomb) — the writing set upon a tomb.

words.definition: A monument honoring people whose remains lie elsewhere.
words.example: The city's cenotaph honors soldiers whose bodies were never recovered from the battlefield.
words.mnemonic: 'Ceno-' (empty) + 'taph' (tomb) — an empty tomb, the body buried somewhere else.

words.definition: Deeply touching, stirring keen feelings of sadness or regret.
words.example: The photograph of the empty playground was a poignant reminder of the children who had moved away.
words.mnemonic: Shares a root with 'point' and 'puncture' — it pierces you right in the heart.

words.definition: Tending to weep easily, or causing others to feel like crying.
words.example: After a few drinks he grew lachrymose, dabbing his eyes over memories of his childhood dog.
words.mnemonic: 'Lachrymal' glands produce tears — a lachrymose person is always near tears.

words.definition: The return or worsening of something harmful after a period of calm or dormancy.
words.example: Doctors feared a recrudescence of the epidemic once the winter crowds packed indoors again.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'crudus' (raw) — think of a wound going 're-crude' again: a scab that reopens and turns raw a second time.

words.definition: Someone who comes back, especially after death or a very long absence.
words.example: He walked into his own funeral reception, a pale revenant startling the mourners into silence.
words.mnemonic: French 'revenir' = to come back (same root as 'revenue', money coming back in). A revenant is one who 'revenirs' — returns from the grave.

words.definition: Impossible to avoid, resist, or escape from.
words.example: As the debts piled higher each month, bankruptcy felt ineluctable, no matter how he juggled the accounts.
words.mnemonic: Latin 'e-' (out) + 'luctari' (to wrestle) — you cannot wrestle your way out of it. Picture being pinned in a wrestling hold you simply can't break.

description: advanced and low-frequency — memory and forgetting
